originalGenerationMetadata.actualAuthorFinding: Mineralsalze are depicted as a pile of solid stones at a direct plant-uptake arrow; replace with dissolved ions in pore water.
originalGenerationMetadata.exactPrompt: Edit this actual SkillPilot soil illustration narrowly. Preserve the friendly comic style, landscape16:9, all main objects, existing short German labels and the correct humus/decomposer branching. Correct only the lower-right Mineralsalze representation: remove the pile of stones completely and replace it with a clearly drawn small pocket of light-blue water in the soil, containing several small uniformly sized coloured circular ion symbols. The existing green uptake arrow must originate in this pore water and point to the plant roots, indicating dissolved mineral nutrients. Keep the large exact German label "Mineralsalze". Show no rocks/crystals being taken up by roots and no mineral nutrients coming from the Sun. Keep every other existing object and label legible. Raster PNG near1600x900, generous contrast; do not add explanations or footnotes.

altDe: Streu und Zersetzer führen zu Humus und gelösten Mineralsalzen im Bodenwasser, die eine Pflanzenwurzel aufnimmt; Sonnenenergie und Wärme werden getrennt dargestellt.
altEn: Litter and decomposers lead to humus and dissolved mineral ions in soil water, taken up by plant roots; sunlight and heat are shown separately.
